links.outcome: Third-party information leakage in LLM-generated notes with a separate privacy-editing step versus single-step generation
links.effect: Separating generation and privacy editing further reduced leakage, but only with contextually specific privacy definitions; no single mitigation eliminated leakage, and combined approaches gave the greatest reductions.
links.quote: Decomposing generation and privacy editing into separate steps could further reduce leakage, but only when privacy was defined with contextual specificity.

unlisted_practices: Adding privacy instructions to ambient scribe note-generation prompts to reduce inclusion of third-party personal information
Combining prompt instructions with a separate privacy-editing step for contextual privacy

screen.practice: privacy prompt instructions and separate privacy-editing step
screen.reason: Evaluates privacy leakage in ambient clinical note generation and tests mitigating practices (privacy-specific prompting and decomposing note generation from privacy editing/filtering steps).

primary.practice: privacy prompt guardrails and multi-step privacy editing
